item.text: The file has three specimens per material, each measured at the same ten strain values. I’ll fit stress against strain separately for each specimen, then report the average specimen slope and its spread so the result reflects replicate variation. The figure will show all measurements and each material’s fit.

item.aggregated_output:
# Tensile test results

Elastic modulus was estimated as the slope of a least-squares linear fit of stress (MPa) against strain for each specimen. The reported modulus is the mean of the three specimen slopes; spread is the sample standard deviation. Fits include a free intercept.

| Material | Elastic modulus (GPa), mean ± SD | Mean specimen-fit R² |
|---|---:|---:|
| Aluminum | 69.38 ± 1.76 | 0.9991 |
| Steel | 199.06 ± 2.00 | 0.9986 |
| Titanium | 116.56 ± 1.71 | 0.9983 |

![Stress–strain measurements and material fits](stress_strain_fits.svg)

The specimens show approximately linear behavior over the measured strain range (0.0002–0.0020). Steel has the highest estimated modulus, followed by titanium and aluminum. The plot shows individual measurements; the colored fit lines are least-squares fits to all measurements for each material. Values are estimates over this test range and may depend on the selected fitting interval.
